result.title: Do learned image captioning metrics generalize? Auditing duplicated samples in human-judgment benchmarks
result.summary: Learned image captioning metrics are trained and tested on human judgments, so their reported correlation is a claim about generalization. We audit this claim for the three most recent collections of such judgments, Polaris, Nebula, and Spica, matching images at the pixel level. First, test samples reappear in training sets: the Spica training set contains about two-thirds of the Polaris test set, with identical human ratings. Second, controlled retraining shows that duplicates can inflate a metric: for Pearl, the gain is confined to the duplicated samples and grows with every epoch; for DENEB, it stays below one point. The gain depends on the learner and on how often a training set repeats a sample. Third, Kendall's $τ$ over all samples is the sum of two terms, detecting captions with the lowest human score and ranking the others; the first supplies most of the reported correlation and is nearly saturated. The recent test sets cannot order Polos, DENEB and Pearl consistently, and a ridge regression on frozen features matches or exceeds all three. Fourth, we propose a protocol that ranks a learned metric only with a model trained without test samples, reports both terms, and compares metrics by paired tests. Under it, zero-shot vision--language judges rank first on the three recent test sets, and a fine-tuned judge ranks first on the three earlier benchmarks. The same analysis applies to any evaluator learned from human judgments; filter lists and code are released at https://github.com/morninghut/ic-dataset-audit .

AI.brief_summary: 论文审计 Polaris、Nebula、Spica 三套人类判断图像描述评测集：通过像素级匹配发现训练/测试重复样本，用受控重训练量化重复样本对学习型指标相关性的虚高，并把 Kendall τ 分解为「识别最差样本」与「其余排序」两项，进而提出排除测试样本、同时报告两分量并做配对检验的评测协议。
AI.relevance_reason: 其泄漏检测、相关性分解与配对检验协议可供核查 LVR 评测中 judge、latent/特征相似度指标的可信度与基准污染，但论文本身不涉及 latent 推理状态。
